directives.text: No Vercel preview deployments. Every non-main deployment must land CANCELED — CANCELED is free, BUILDING/READY/ERROR is billed.
A push is the only Actions-consuming action a push approval covers. Reruns, workflow_dispatch, a second push or a non-draft PR are each a fresh ask.
A commit hash AND a verification that ran AND a user-invocable outcome. Two of three is not done.
A gate that cannot fail is not a gate. Prove it fails before trusting that it passed, and take exit codes from UNPIPED commands.
A record of a thing is not the thing. Measure the artefact, not the comment, filename or tracker row describing it.
This board is DERIVED from the release tracker and defect register. Where they disagree with it, THEY WIN.

MANDATORY for every release, every session: start by reading this board. Be able to state total raised, how many are done, and of the rest how many are not started / written-awaiting-certification / awaiting an owner decision — INCLUDING which population each number belongs to. The headline counts and the per-phase counts measure different things; subtracting one from the other gives a wrong answer.

At release close every item goes to exactly ONE place: still pending (not started, built, or awaiting a decision) HANDS OVER to the next release with its evidence; done and cleared are SAVED AS RELEASE DELIVERY. The board then re-points at the new release. Nothing is dropped at a boundary. See docs/STATUS-BOARD-CHARTER.md.

If a status cannot express the truth, ADD THE STATE — never pick the nearest wrong one. Twice this release a status was falsified by a missing word: built-but-not-shipped read as FIXED, and withdrawn read as OPEN forever. A phantom OPEN is as damaging as a phantom FIXED.

crowagent-website is SEPARATE. It does not count against that budget and ships as and when ready.
Railway, staging AND production: deploy whenever needed. No approval, no waiting.
Supabase, staging AND production: apply whenever needed. No approval, no waiting. Via MCP apply_migration, never db push.
There is no Phase 5. Phase 2 is CLOSED. Every remaining item is Phase 3 or Phase 4.
Never report deploy or phase state from a repository document or git log. Read the live surface — Vercel, Stripe, Supabase, Railway.

issues.title: [SEV:P0] Northern Ireland is INSIDE the Procurement Act 2023 and the registry says otherwise
issues.note: The jurisdiction registry declares ppr_2016 for NI and cites a REVOKED SI (2015/102), carrying wrong thresholds, the wrong award basis (MEAT where the Act says MAT) and the wrong standstill. This one reaches the SELLER product, which DOES consume the registry - so it is not a buyer-only paper defect. Adding or correcting a jurisdiction is "a ruleset plus a source and no engine change" by the registry's own design, so the fix is data, not engine. Sourced from primary legislation, a URL per claim. The audit was RIGHT on substance and WRONG on two citations, both corrected in the YAML so they cannot propagate: SI 2025/163 did NOT revoke PCR 2015 (the Act's own s.127(2)/Sch.11 para.5 did), and s.112 is NOT a disapplication list (s.84(2) is) - the audit's s.13/s.53(3)/s.69 claims were therefore NOT asserted. A FOURTH CHANGE NOBODY PREDICTED: NI contracts were being REFUSED HTTP 409 for a competitive-flexible-procedure sequence - the product was BLOCKING A PROCEDURE NI AUTHORITIES ARE ENTITLED TO RUN. Finding it exposed a SECOND SOURCE OF TRUTH: _REGIMES_SUPPORTING_USER_DEFINED_STAGES claimed in its own comment to mirror regime-config.ts and be "locked by tests", and the test hardcoded the same literal on BOTH sides - so it could never catch the divergence it was named for. The England/Wales window runs to 2027-12-31, so this is a data-staleness defect with a live blast radius in two jurisdictions, not a design flaw. This is the runtime half: describe_ruleset_coverage() now returns thresholds_are_current, computed rather than stored, so no surface re-derives the comparison differently. Unknown is never reported as in force - a missing window returns False, because a missing window reading as "in force" would present figures of unknown vintage as though they had been checked. The boundary day is asserted, since an off-by-one would call a jurisdiction expired on the last day its figures are law. No regulated value was invented: this compares a date to today, and Scotland's figures remain expired and remain recorded as debt.

issues.title: [SEV:P0] the 10% social-value floor is a hard PUBLISH BLOCK for every buyer, including the ones it does not bind
issues.note: The floor is mandatory in exactly THREE places: central government, NHS (by NHSE policy, not law) and Northern Ireland. It is NOT mandatory for councils, universities, colleges, schools, housing associations, police, fire, Scotland or Wales - yet it blocks publication for all of them, including the archetypal council user. The blocking message also cites PPN 06/20, which is superseded. Two defects in one control: it applies a rule to bodies it does not bind, and cites the wrong authority while doing it. The floor now binds only the three bodies it reaches, each carrying its OWN instrument rather than one flat rule: central_government under PPN 002 (mandatory 1 Oct 2025), nhs under NHS England policy (April 2022, deliberately NOT attributed to PPN 002, which does not reach trusts or ICBs), and any public body in Northern Ireland under DoF PPN 01/21. Councils, education and housing associations resolve to ADVISORY, a real duty to consider with no percentage. The superseded PPN 06/20 citation is replaced everywhere. crp_required is carried as its OWN rule set, and the data proves that is necessary: central government has a mandatory floor and no asserted CRP duty while the NHS has both. NI's rule has NO WRITER and says so - no buyer surface captures jurisdiction, verified against production, so the resolver returns the rule id as UNEVALUATED rather than silently not applying it.
